title: Write all terms in base $$3$$.
text:
$$3**{2x-3}+9**{x-1}=27**{x-2}$$ 
 Notice that the bases and exponents are different. But all bases are powers of $$3$$, so we can write everything in terms of base $$3$$. 

$$3**{2x-3}+(3**2)**{x-1}=(3**3)**{x-2}$$

title: Apply the laws of exponentiation for powers
LHS Pull out a factor of $$3**{2x-3}$$
text:
There is no exponential rule for sums of exponential expressions. To combine the two terms on the left-hand side, we look for a common factor $$a**{b+c}=a**b a**c.$$ Rewrite the left hand side as 
 $$3**{2x-3}+3**{2(x-1)}=3**{2x-3}+3**{2x-2)}$$ 
 $$=3**{2x-3}+3**{2x-3+1}=3**{2x-3}+(3**{2x-3})(3**1)$$ 
 $$=3**{2x-3}(1+3)$$

title: Put it together
text: Plugging this into the left-hand side of the equation, we get \n $$3**{2x-3}(1+3)=3**{3(x-2)}$$

title: Apply the laws of logarithms
text:
Apply the law of logarithms for products $$\log_c(ab)=\log_c(a)+\log_c(b)$$ to the left-hand side. 
 $$\log_3(3**{2x-3}(4))=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)})$$ 
 becomes 
 $$\log_3(3**{2x-3})+\log_3(4)=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)})$$

title: Apply the cancellation principle
text:
$$\log_b(b**a)=a$$ 
 Log base $$3$$ undoes exponentiation with base $$3$$. So the equation $$\log_3(3**{2x-3})+\log_3(4)=\log_3(3**{3(x-2)})$$ reduces to 

$$2x-3+\log_3(4)=3(x-2)$$.
